name: Azaniah
overview: Azaniah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Jeshua. His role is noted in the context of post-exilic Israel, highlighting his lineage within the Levitical priestly tribe. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Azaniah means 'YHWH has listened,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name that acknowledges God's attentive nature. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:9 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azaniah as the father of Jeshua, as noted in Nehemiah 10:9. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Azaniah's significance lies in his connection to Jeshua, a key figure in the restoration of Israel's worship after the exile. As a Levite and father of Jeshua, Azaniah represents the continuity of the priestly line entrusted with maintaining covenant faithfulness. His mention in Nehemiah underscores the importance of genealogical records in affirming the legitimacy of Israel's religious leaders during the post-exilic period.
